[LEXP.3.7.1] Members of an `Int` value ([LGRA.9.6.2]). Each reads `x` as its
64-bit two's-complement pattern ([LEXP.7.13.1]), bit 0 being the least
significant.

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `x.bit_count` | the number of 1 bits in the pattern; `-1` has 64 |
| `x.bit_length` | the number of bits $\lvert x \rvert$ needs, as Python's `int.bit_length`; 0 for 0 |
| `x.leading_zeros` | the number of 0 bits above the highest 1 bit; 64 for 0, and 0 for a negative `x` ([LEXP.3.7.3]) |
| `x.trailing_zeros` | the number of 0 bits below the lowest 1 bit; 64 for 0 ([LEXP.3.7.3]) |
| `x.bits(lo, width)` | the `width` bits from bit `lo` upward ([LEXP.3.7.3]) |
| `x.sign_extend(width)` | the low `width` bits, read as a two's-complement number ([LEXP.3.7.3]) |
| `x.swap_bytes(width)` | the low `width / 8` bytes, in reverse order ([LEXP.3.7.3]) |
